story: Orpheus, son of the Thracian king Oeagrus and the Muse Calliope, was a legendary musician, poet, and prophet. Apollo gave him a golden lyre and taught him to play, while his mother taught him to make verses. His music could charm birds, fish, and wild beasts, move trees and rocks to dance, and divert rivers. Orpheus joined Jason and the Argonauts in search of the Golden Fleece. When the ship passed the Sirens, whose songs lured sailors to wreck on rocky islands, Orpheus played his lyre louder and more beautifully, drowning out their voices and saving the crew. Later, Orpheus married Eurydice. While walking among her people at her wedding, she was pursued by a satyr and fled into a nest of vipers, dying from a fatal bite. Grief-stricken, Orpheus played such mournful songs that nymphs and gods wept. He traveled to the underworld, where his music softened the hearts of its rulers, who agreed to let Eurydice return with him on the condition that he walk ahead and not look back until both reached the upper world. As Orpheus emerged, he turned to look at her too soon, before she had crossed over, and she vanished forever. Toward the end of his life, Orpheus abandoned worship of other gods, honoring only the sun as the greatest deity. Rising early to greet the sunrise atop a mountain, he angered his former patron, who sent frenzied female worshippers to tear him limb from limb. He was buried afterward, his death mirroring that of another figure similarly destroyed by the same maddened women.
